data.tombstone: Wannian Bridge in Suzhou (姑蘇萬年橋), 1741. China, Qing dynasty (1644–1911), Qianlong reign (1736–95). Hanging scroll; polychrome woodblock print; ink and color on paper; print only: 102.3 x 54 cm (40 1/4 x 21 1/4 in.); overall: 176.5 x 57.4 cm (69 1/2 x 22 5/8 in.); with knobs: 176.5 x 62.5 cm (69 1/2 x 24 5/8 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund, 2025.80

data.did_you_know: Woodblock printing in color reached a height in China in the 1600s to 1700s. The prints were executed by means of sets of separate blocks, each carved to print a different color.
data.description: In the 1600s, printing flourished in such Jiangnan cities as Nanjing, Suzhou, Hangzhou, and Huizhou, evolving from privately enjoyed illustrated books printed in color to more commercialized single-sheet color prints that were hung on walls and became part of the rich urban visual culture.
